```python
import re

def text_match_one(text):
    return bool(re.search(r'ab+', text))
```

This keeps the earlier pattern, `ab+`, which matches an `a` followed by one or more `b`s anywhere in the string. The note's `ab+?` also works here, because `re.search` only needs one `b` to match, but `ab+` is the standard form. `text_match_one("ac")` returns `False`, and `text_match_one("abba")` returns `True`.
